main_text.p: mine aliquid emerit. ita denique accipiendum, vt cum ait Ariftoteles in fecundo Oeconomicorum de Cleomene Alexandrino loquens, ἀποσείλας δέ [?] τινα ὅτι ἀγόρασμά τι, αἰσθόμενος, ὅτι ἐώνων τετύχηκε, ἀπὸ ᾧ μέλλῃ ἐκλελογισμένα λογίζεσθαι. Diuus Paulus etiam ἐλλογεῖν hoc sensu solet vsurpare. Appianus καταλογίζειν.

ἡ οἰκέτου χύτραν ἢ λοπάδα καταξαίνων.] Bellè hæc cōueniunt Athenienfibus: quos in rebus ita minutis & parui pretij mirè fuiffe attentos & follicitos, nequid sibi seruorum fraude periret, Ariftophanis fabulæ testantur. Nam in Ranis ait poëta plerosq; Athenienfium statim vbi domum fuerint ingressi, nihil antiquius habere, quàm vt seruos suos magno cum clamore appellent, & ab ipsis scifcitetur, quid olla factum esset, quid capite mænadis quæ forte fuerat è mensa sublata: quid paropside anno superiore empta: quid pridiano allio; quis denique de oleis deguftarit. page.notes: The Greek of the first line of the second paragraph (ἡ οἰκέτου χύτραν ἢ λοπάδα καταξαίνων) and the verse lines are hard to read at this scan resolution; check them against the original. The Greek in the first paragraph (ἀποσείλας, ἐώνων, ἐκλελογισμένα) is uncertain. The Scholiastes paragraph's Greek words may be set in italic in the print; I have left them in roman. The page ends mid-word with the hyphen "δείγ-", which continues on the next page. No catchword is printed.
